title: eval-harness: prompt-regression CI enhancements and per-prompt thresholds
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: we frequently see noisy eval CI runs where a small subset of prompts cause intermittent score drops; teams need per-prompt sensitivity and deterministic gating to avoid both false positives and missed regressions. This PR adds per-prompt thresholding, improved metrics reporting, and CI hooks that fail builds on sustained regressions.

Summary of changes: - Introduce per-prompt threshold config and precedence rules (global -> suite -> prompt) - Enforce threshold checks in the eval-harness CI step; support soft-fail mode for flaky suites - Add a lightweight metrics reporter that emits per-prompt delta and alertable tags to build artifacts - Wire new gating into the GitHub Actions eval job and expose a CLI flag for local runs (--enforce-thresholds / --soft-fail) - Add unit+integration tests that simulate regressions, and new test fixtures for prompt-level baselines - Update docs: CI troubleshooting and how to configure per-prompt overrides

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear tasks linked (ENG-2145) - [x] Unit tests for threshold logic - [x] Integration tests for CI hook - [x] Docs for maintainers and runbook - [x] Backwards-compatible: default behavior preserved when no thresholds defined

Rollout plan: Merge to main; enable enforcement in a staged manner for critical suites only (controlled via repo-level feature flag). After 2 weeks of stability, flip enforcement on for all eval suites. Teams can opt out by adding `soft_fail: true` to their suite config.

Why now: We've had two incidents in the past quarter where downstream deploys were delayed because of noisy eval failures. Per-prompt gating reduces noise and reduces manual triage.

Notes: The description above is intentionally concise; see the linked Linear tasks for full acceptance criteria.
